Interpretation: We have 13 distinct red balls (say R1,...,R13) and 7 distinct blue balls (B1,...,B7). We consider all unordered pairs of balls from the combined set of 20 balls. There are total number of unordered pairs = C(20,2) = 190. Among these, we discard those pairs that contain two blue balls. How many such pairs? Number of ways to choose 2 blue balls from 7 = C(7,2) = 21. So remaining pairs = 190 - 21 = 169.

Now among these remaining pairs, we want the fraction that contain two red balls. That is: number of pairs that are both red (i.e., choose 2 red balls from 13) divided by total remaining pairs (169). Number of red-red pairs = C(13,2) = 78. So fraction = 78 / 169.
